resources.string: Normal midsagittal anatomy, with the front of the brain at left. Teal marks the hypothalamus. Regional schematic, not to scale.
The hypothalamus lies below and partly in front of the thalamus. It forms the floor and part of the lower walls of the third ventricle.
The thalamus lies above and partly behind the hypothalamus. The hypothalamic sulcus marks their boundary along the wall of the third ventricle.
Some optic nerve fibers cross here, at the base of the brain in front of the pituitary stalk.
The infundibulum descends from the floor of the hypothalamus and is continuous with the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland.
